stem: A dataset of 40 values is grouped into 5 equal-width classes starting at 0. The cumulative frequencies are: up to 10 = 6, up to 20 = 16, up to 30 = 30, up to 40 = 38, up to 50 = 40. Which class interval contains the median?

per_option_rationale.rationale: N = 40, so the median is the average of the 20th and 21st values. Cumulative frequency up to 20 is 16 (< 20) and up to 30 is 30 (>= 20). Both the 20th and 21st values fall in [20-30].

Cumulative frequency up to 20 is 16; the student confused the class just before the median class with the median class itself, picking [10-20] because its cumulative frequency is closest to but still below N/2.
[30-40] contains the 31st through 38th values; the 20th and 21st are not in this range.
[0-10] contains only the first 6 values; the median at position 20.5 is far beyond this class.

explanation: For N = 40, the median position is N/2 = 20. The cumulative frequency first exceeds 20 in the class [20-30] (cumulative frequency reaches 30 at the end of that class, after being 16 at the end of [10-20]). Therefore the median lies in [20-30].

explanation_sections.punchline: Median class = the first class whose cumulative frequency reaches or exceeds N/2 = 20; that class is [20-30].
explanation_sections.approach: Identify the model: locate the median class from cumulative frequencies. Compute N/2 = 20. Find the class where cumulative frequency first >= 20: cf up to 20 is 16 (< 20), cf up to 30 is 30 (>= 20) -> median class is [20-30].
explanation_sections.lesson: The median class is identified by finding the first class whose cumulative frequency is >= N/2, not by the class containing exactly the N/2-th value marker from a raw list.
explanation_sections.timing: 90 s. N/2 = 20; scan cumulative: 6, 16, 30 - first time >= 20 is at 30, belonging to [20-30].
